title: Geometric sections of a finite Weil scheme and the local return operators
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0=\mathbf F_q,k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $Z_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], put $Z=Z_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal G$ be a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $Z_0$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex, def-weil-constructible-heart]. Write $V=H_c^0(Z,\mathcal G)$ for geometric compactly supported cohomology [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], with its geometric Frobenius $F$ [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], interpreted at a common finite coefficient-field stage as in the Weil-sheaf definition. For a closed point $x\in|Z_0|$, put $d_x=[\kappa(x):k_0]$ and let $P_x$ be the set of $k$-morphisms $z:\operatorname{Spec}k\to Z$ whose projection to $Z_0$ has image $x$. Let $\mathcal G_z$ denote the geometric stalk at $z$, and let $F_{x,z}$ be its degree-$d_x$ local geometric-Frobenius operator [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], also extended from a common finite coefficient-field stage.

The set $|Z_0|$ is finite, $|P_x|=d_x\geq1$, and evaluation on geometric stalks gives a $\Qlb$-linear isomorphism
$$e:V\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{x\in|Z_0|}\ \bigoplus_{z\in P_x}\mathcal G_z.$$
The vector space $V$ is finite-dimensional and $F$ is an automorphism. Under $e$, $F$ preserves each summand $V_x=\bigoplus_{z\in P_x}\mathcal G_z$ and permutes its stalk summands cyclically, by linear isomorphisms. If $e_z:V\to\mathcal G_z$ is the component of $e$, then
$$e_z\circ F^{d_x}=F_{x,z}\circ e_z\qquad(z\in P_x).$$
The evaluation isomorphism is natural for morphisms of constructible Weil sheaves. No reducedness of $Z_0$ and no weight or semisimplicity hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-finite-geometric-sections-and-point-orbits] to the underlying constructible sheaf of $\mathcal G$. It supplies the finite sets, $|P_x|=d_x\geq1$, finite-dimensionality, the natural evaluation isomorphism $e$, and the cycles $T(z)=gzh^{-1}$, with $g^{d_x}z=zh^{d_x}$. Naturality for all underlying sheaf maps restricts to Weil-sheaf morphisms.

proof.text: The finite structure morphism is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], so [lem-a1-proper-weil-iterate-germ-formula] applies with $Y_0=Z_0$ and $K=\mathcal G$ in degree zero. Its $r=1$ identity, after $\mathrm H^0$, is $e_zF=B_{1,z}e_{Tz}$, where each $B_{1,z}:\mathcal G_{Tz}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal G_z$ is an isomorphism. Consequently conjugation by $e$ gives exactly one invertible block in output $z$, from input $Tz$. Since $T$ is one cycle on $P_x$, this preserves $V_x$ and cyclically permutes its stalk summands in direction $T^{-1}$.

source.place: First sentence and displayed evaluation formula, corrected to geometric stalks and explicit Frobenius return; assembly after the 2026-10-22 re-split

proof.text: For $z\in P_x$, the return from step 1 is $T^{d_x}z=z$ and $g^{d_x}z=zh^{d_x}$. The returning-point assertion of [lem-a1-proper-weil-iterate-germ-formula], with $r=d_x$, therefore gives $e_zF^{d_x}=F_{x,z}e_z$ after $\mathrm H^0$. Its three factors are the iterated point transport, the specified return comparison and the pulled-back iterated Weil map; thus it uses exactly the local-operator convention in the statement. All these formulas and $e$ extend from the same common coefficient-field stage.

proof.text: For completeness, the block operator from step 2 has inverse given in output $Tz$ by $B_{1,z}^{-1}$ applied to input $z$. The two composites are identities on every summand, hence on their finite sum. Conjugating by $e$ makes $F$ an automorphism. If $Z_0$ is empty, both sums and $V$ are zero, and the same argument gives the unique automorphism of the zero space.
